The build succeeded. The fix was:

1. Added `guava-android` and `failureaccess` to the version catalog
2. Added both as explicit dependencies in `build.gradle.kts`
3. Added a resolution strategy to force the Android variant of Guava
4. Added ProGuard/R8 rules for Guava

The root cause was that `health-connect-client` (or another transitive dependency) pulled in the JRE variant of Guava (`com.google.guava:guava:33.x.x-jre`), and when R8 ran with `isMinifyEnabled = true`, it couldn't process `com.google.common.util.concurrent.Uninterruptibles` because the JRE variant references JDK classes not available on Android.

The fix ensures the Android-compatible variant (`com.google.guava:guava:33.6.0-android`) is used instead, which replaces those problematic classes with Android-compatible implementations.

Build passed. Here's what was wrong and what I fixed:

**Root cause:** The `health-connect-client` library pulls in Guava's JRE variant as a transitive dependency. With `isMinifyEnabled = true`, R8 processes all classes and chokes on `Uninterruptibles` — the JRE Guava variant references JDK internals that don't exist on Android.

**Fix (3 changes):**

1. **`gradle/libs.versions.toml`** — Added explicit `guava` (33.6.0-android) and `failureaccess` (1.0.3) dependencies so Gradle uses the Android-compatible Guava variant instead of the JRE one.

2. **`app/build.gradle.kts`** — Added both dependencies, plus a `resolutionStrategy.force()` to prevent any transitive dependency from overriding with the JRE variant.

3. **`app/proguard-rules.pro`** — Added R8/ProGuard `-dontwarn` rules for Guava's annotation dependencies (`errorprone`, `j2objc`, `checkerframework`, `javax.annotation`) that aren't needed at runtime.
